overview: This file concerns restrictions and conditions governing alien labor and employment in Japanese-ruled Taiwan (Formosa). Its principal document is a November 1932 consular report stating that Taiwan had no laws restricting aliens’ employment, although the entry of Chinese laborers was controlled through licenses issued under the Government General’s “Regulations Governing Control of Chinese Laborers.” The file also contains cross-reference sheets directing researchers to the original despatch and to a November 1934 Tokyo despatch about labor conditions and rules for the temporary admission and residence of foreign musicians, artists, actors, choristers, and other workers.

subfiles.title: Report on alien employment restrictions in Taiwan
subfiles.from: John H. Ketcham, U.S. Consul at Taihoku
subfiles.about: The report explains that Taiwan imposed no restrictions on aliens’ employment but regulated the immigration of Chinese laborers.
subfiles.summary: 1932 report finds no Taiwanese law restricted alien employment, though Chinese laborers needed government-issued entry licenses before facing no further employment restriction, citing Government General sources.
